Cusco · Perú

Saint Peter’s Church, Andahuaylillas

Painted walls behind a quiet rural façade

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

A modest frontage facing the town square gives little warning of the painted interior. Wall paintings, ceiling decoration and liturgical furnishings were conceived for a parish church. View them as an ensemble before approaching any particular image.

Planning your visit

40–60 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

Painted walls behind a quiet rural façade

The plaza gives the best context for the modest exterior. Inside, put the camera away whenever the parish requires it and follow the painted surfaces with your eyes from wall to ceiling.

History and local experience

The surface decoration draws the eye from wall to ceiling. Pause well back in the permitted area first, then focus on a single panel as part of the larger parish interior.

Walking route

  1. Plaza de Andahuaylillas, Quispicanchi
  2. Start in the plaza, walk to the raised church forecourt and check the parish visitor entrance.
  3. Follow the authorised interior circuit; photography rules may be different inside and outside.
